paper.title: Top-$k$ Pareto Bandits: Hypervolume Regret for Multi-Objective Slate Selection

settings.name_in_paper: Top-k Pareto bandits (multi-objective top-k semi-bandit with hypervolume alpha-regret)
unmapped: Multi-objective: each arm yields a d-dimensional reward vector in [0,1]^d (d = number of objectives, recorded as d_obj)
Reward of a slate is the dominated hypervolume of the selected arms' mean vectors w.r.t. a reference point r dominated by all means (r known to the learner)
Regret is the alpha-approximation regret alpha*V* - HV(S_t) with alpha = 1-1/e against the best size-k subset
Each reward coordinate is eta-sub-Gaussian; eta is also used as the algorithm's confidence parameter
Action = any subset of size k of n arms
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in[T]$, the agent selects a subset $S_t\subseteq[n]$ of size $|S_t|=k$ (a \emph{slate}) and observes the vectors $\{\mathbf{X}_{i,t}: i\in S_t\}$ (semi-bandit feedback). ... $\bar{r}_t = \alpha V^\star - \mathrm{HV}(S_t), \quad \bar{R}_T = \sum_{t=1}^{T} \bar{r}_t.$

symbols.C_d: coordinate-wise Lipschitz constant of the hypervolume; C_d <= d_obj when rewards in [0,1]^d and r = 0

conditions: each reward coordinate is eta-sub-Gaussian and bounded in [0,1]
holds on the event E where all confidence intervals hold, P(E) >= 1 - delta
tuning: beta_i(t) = sqrt(2 eta log(n d t^2/delta)/N_i(t-1))

source.label: thm:gapfree
source.quote: Assume each reward coordinate is $\eta$-sub-Gaussian and bounded in $[0,1]$. On $\mathcal{E}$, \[ \bar{R}_T \;=\; O\!\left( C_d \sqrt{n k T \log T} \right). \]

results.notes: Regret is the alpha-approximation (alpha=1-1/e) hypervolume regret. Paper's n = K (arms), k = m (slate size). Detailed version Theorem 4 (thm:gap-free) restates the same bound. Abstract states O~(d sqrt(nkT)) using C_d <= d. log(1/delta) dependence hidden in O.

symbols.Delta_min_stage: minimum stage-wise gap of the greedy benchmark G* on true means: min over stages l and arms i != i*_l of Delta(i*_l | G*_{l-1}) - Delta(i | G*_{l-1})

conditions: each reward coordinate is eta-sub-Gaussian and bounded in [0,1]
the greedy maximizer of G* is unique at every stage
the safe-pruning step never eliminates an arm of G*
holds on the event E, P(E) >= 1 - delta
tuning: beta_i(t) = sqrt(2 eta log(n d t^2/delta)/N_i(t-1))

source.label: thm:gapdep
source.quote: Under the same assumptions, if the greedy maximizer of $G^\star$ is unique at every stage and the safe-pruning step never eliminates an arm of $G^\star$, then on $\mathcal{E}$, \[ \bar{R}_T \;=\; O\!\left( \frac{n k^{2.5} \log T}{\Delta_{\min}} \right). \]

results.notes: alpha-approximation hypervolume regret. Delta_min is a greedy stage-wise gap, not the usual arm gap. Pruning condition is assumed, not proved (footnote). Detailed version Theorem 5 identical.

bound.expression_latex: \min\Bigl\{ O\left(\sqrt{n k T \log T}\right), O\left(\frac{n k^{2.5} \log T}{\Delta_{\min}}\right) \Bigr\} + O(1)

symbols.Delta_min_stage: minimum stage-wise gap of the greedy benchmark G* on true means

conditions: each reward coordinate is eta-sub-Gaussian and bounded in [0,1]
gap-dependent term requires unique greedy maximizer at every stage and pruning never eliminating an arm of G*

source.label: thm:combined
source.quote: With $\delta = 1/T$, \mathbb{E}\big[\bar{R}_T\big] \leq \min\Bigl\{ O\left(\sqrt{n k T \log T}\right), O\left(\frac{n k^{2.5} \log T}{\Delta_{\min}}\right) \Bigr\} + O(1). In particular $\mathbb{E}[\bar{R}_T]/T \to 0$

results.notes: Expected alpha-approximation (alpha=1-1/e) hypervolume pseudo-regret (defined through means). C_d is dropped in this statement (treated as constant). Detailed version Theorem 8 (thm:main) identical.
